headline: Showers ease Saturday, then cool, clear nights bring the first frost; light rain returns Tuesday.
summary: A weak low pressure system is moving across western Washington, bringing scattered showers through Saturday afternoon with highs in the mid to upper 50s. Gusty winds are easing and skies should clear Saturday evening. Clear, light-wind nights will let temperatures drop fast, to the mid 40s around Seattle and the mid 30s in sheltered valleys. The first Frost Advisory of the season covers valleys and foothills south of Seattle, and fog near Olympia could complicate frost there. Sunday and Monday look mostly dry, with highs in the low 60s and possible frost again Sunday night. Light rain is expected Tuesday into Wednesday, though its timing has shifted later. After midweek the pattern is uncertain, but milder, high-pressure weather is favored.
changes: The evening discussion pushed the midweek rain later than earlier forecasts. It also said the frost advisory could expand to other areas if conditions change.
